34 BC: 'The fourth and final conflict occurred 34–33 BC during Octavian's expedition to Illyricum' (Dalmatae page).

33 BC: 'Upon his own death in 33 BC, Bocchus II bequeathed his entire kingdom to Octavian'; 'Octavian placed Mauretania under temporary Roman administration for eight years' (Mauretania page, reopened eu-03-b-fix 2026-10-19). The page gives no boundary for 33; the shape is Cliopatria's Mauretania of 27. Drawn as tint (rule 4); mauretania.json /ledger/9 and 10 make it a client of Rome from 33 to 25 BC. No vassal_end here: the relation outlives the Republic (January 27).
33 BC: the Roman-Dalmatae wars 'lasted until 33 BC when Octavian' installed Roman hegemony.

33 BC: Octavian ends Dalmatian independence (dalmatae.json /ledger/8). The page places the Dalmatae in 'southern Croatia and western Bosnia and Herzegovina'; the later revolts (12 BC, AD 6-9) fall outside this dossier.
32 BC: the occupation lapses: 'the Romans lost hegemony during the Final War of the Roman Republic in 32-30 BC'.

32 BC: the 66 BC client relation ends: 'the Romans lost hegemony during the Final War of the Roman Republic in 32-30 BC'; in 20 BC Augustus made Armenia 'a buffer zone between the two major powers'. The page gives 66 ('Armenia became a Roman client kingdom in 66 BC') and 34 but no year for Artavasdes II's turn to Parthia, so the tint runs 66-32.

31 BC: Cyprus returns to Rome. 'Battle of Actium, Marc Antony and Cleopatra were defeated by Augustus and Cyprus returns to Roman rule'; 'resulting in Octavian gaining control of all of Egypt and Cyprus'; 'Cyprus was left under control of Octavian's legate until it could be further dealt with' (Roman Cyprus page, reopened eu-03-b-fix 2026-10-19). Actium itself was on 2 September.

31 BC: Thrace under Sapaean clients. 'Probably soon after the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, Roman leader Augustus sought to implement indirect rule over Thrace'; the Odrysian-Astaean royal family removed and 'the entire kingdom under Sapaean rule with Bizye acting as the initial center'. Actium itself (2 September 31) moved no Republican border; Cyprus (31), Egypt (August 30) and Cilicia Aspera (30) are separate events and keyframes of their own, because they fall inside the dossier's life (it ends in January 27).

30 BC: Cilicia Aspera (bridging a silence). 'Marcus Antonius ... gave Cyprus and Cilicia Aspera to Cleopatra VII' in 36 and 'Augustus placed this territory under the rule of king Archelaus of Cappadocia in 25 BC' (Cilicia page, reopened eu-03-b-fix 2026-10-19); the page says nothing about who held it between Actium and 25, so Octavian's control from Cleopatra's fall is the researcher's reading.

August 30 BC: Egypt. 'In August 30 BC, following the Battle of Alexandria (30 BC) the defeated Antony and Cleopatra killed themselves. The Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt ceased to exist; Egypt was seized by Octavian as his personal possession' (Egypt (Roman province) page, opened eu-03-b-fix 2026-10-19); 'The legal status was settled in January 27 BC, when ... Egypt became an imperial province'. Cliopatria's Ptolemaic Kingdom shape of 30-28 (554,000 km2) is Egypt. Drawn here as the Republic's last gain, Octavian's personal holding handed to the Empire in 27.

notes:
Roman Republic, Phase B group eu-03, written 2026-10-18 from the 53 pages listed.

Shared Wikidata id: 'Revolutionary Roman Republic' (1799, Q175881) is the Jacobin republic of 1798-1799, a different state; its row stays with the European 18th-century group. Cliopatria rows corrected here: the Republic begins 509 (not 500) and the Roman Kingdom row's 500-481 shape belongs to it; it ends in January 27 (not 32), while the Roman Empire row starts in 31: the roman-empire group should start at 27 or the compiler must hand over at 31. The '(Allegiance of Seleucid Empire to Roman Republic)' relation row (203-189) has no support on the pages opened (Magnesia 190, Apamea 188: indemnity and territorial losses to Pergamon and Rhodes, not vassalage). Cliopatria's biggest errors: Numidia drawn as Roman in 212-198 (Syphax and Masinissa were allies), the Regulus expedition drawn as territory 256-248, Sardinia and Corsica eight years late (230 for 238), Cisalpine Gaul kept two years after it rose for Hannibal (216 for 218), Macedon two years early (170 for 168) and as direct rule in the merides years, an eastern edge in Anatolia 164-145, Asia kept out 87-78 after its recovery in 85, Armenia drawn as Roman 66-64, Gaul added all at once in 50, Syria kept lost to 37 after its recovery in 38, Cyprus apparently kept after 47.

States Cliopatria lacks that this ledger names as counterparts (dossiers written in this batch where marked *): samnites*, latin-league*, syracuse*, lucanians*, umbri*, senones*, boii*, insubres*, adriatic-veneti*, celtiberians*, lusitanians*, volsci*, aequi*, sabines*, picentes*, sertorian-hispania* (rebel, 80-72), plus the Kingdom of Epirus (Pyrrhus, 280-272; Cliopatria has only 'Molossians' 170-165 and the '(Macedonian Empire)' umbrella), Gentius' Illyrian kingdom of 168 (the 'Illyrian Kingdom' row ends 226), the Bruttii, the Messapii/Sallentini, the Marsi-Paeligni-Marrucini-Frentani-Vestini (treated as one allied group), the Pompeian faction of 49-45 (not a state), Eumenes III's Pergamene revolt (133-129), the Arverni-Allobroges and the Gallic tribes of 58-50 (named as a group), the Cilician pirates. Counterparts with rows: carthage, etruscans, greek-city-states (used for the Italiote Greeks, Massilia and Crete: that row spans 883 years and should be split), illyrian-kingdom, antigonid-dynasty (Cliopatria Antigonid Macedonia), molossians, achaean-league, aetolian-league, kingdom-of-pergamon, kingdom-of-numidia, cyrenaica (row ends 92; the bequest was 96 and the province 74), kingdom-of-bithynia, kingdom-of-pontus, kingdom-of-cappadocia, kingdom-of-armenia, seleucid-empire, judea, galatia, ptolemaic-kingdom, parthian-empire, thracian-kingdom, mamertines, italian-city-states.
